name: WILLIS LEASE FINANCE

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That I am refusing the same name for the third time on a defect rather than engaging the business, and the business is good: 98th percentile of 151 Industrials, lease rent compounding, AUM $4.4bn, and the market apparently requiring only +6%. If the WACC is genuinely 14.38% too high and the true discount rate is nearer 7%, the name is substantially cheap even on a halved cash-flow base.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: A clean reading of maintenance versus growth fleet investment. Willis does not split them, and the AROC rule says a base struck after TOTAL fleet capex must be paired with the growth that capex buys - which for a lessor is most of the growth.
devils_advocate.already_visible: The two corrections are visible, measurable, and run opposite ways: capex alone takes the requirement to +19.4%, the WACC alone to -13.6%. That is the SM condition exactly, and the 2026-09-09 pass on this name predicted the gap 'does not shrink, it inverts' - which was the one-sided answer and was wrong.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Whether gains on sale of leased equipment, $32.0M in Q2 against $34.0M of total income from operations, are recurring income or portfolio liquidation. For a lessor that is the difference between a 6% grower and a melting ice cube, and the filings do not separate maintenance from growth fleet spend to settle it.

what_changed: Nothing that changes the valuation question, which is itself the point. Q2 2026 (filed 2026-08-04): income from operations $34.0M +20.2%, lease rent $77.1M +6.7%, core lease rent and maintenance reserve revenue $123.6M +0.5%, gain on sale of leased equipment $32.0M +16.2%, net income to common $28.7M, adjusted EBITDA $120.7M +4.0%, AUM $4.4bn - all materially the same picture recorded on 2026-09-23. Since then: an investor presentation at Deutsche Aviation Finance on 2026-09-08; on 2026-09-16 (announced 2026-09-22) a $35M preferred stock purchase agreement with Development Bank of Japan for 1,750,000 shares of 8.09% Series B Preferred, cited as supporting global expansion including a new Willis Engine Repair Center in Johor, Malaysia; and a 2026-09-30 8-K under item 5.03 amending the articles, consistent with creating that Series B. New preferred at 8.09% is a datapoint on the cost of capital and is dilutive to the common's claim, but none of it moves the base case. I found no filing explaining the -10% five-day move that won the opportunistic slot.
consensus_case: Willis Lease is compounding an engine portfolio into the tightest aftermarket in commercial aviation history: assets under management reached $4.4bn, Q2 lease rent revenue $77.1M was up 6.7%, income from operations $34.0M up 20.2%, adjusted EBITDA $120.7M up 4.0%, and gains on sale of leased equipment $32.0M up 16.2%. Engine shortages from GTF powder-metal inspections and CFM LEAP production constraints have made spare CFM56 and V2500 capacity scarce and lease rates high, and Willis is one of very few independent lessors with the portfolio to supply it. At $47.80 the market requires something like +6% five-year FCFF growth on the engine's own numbers, which is less than lease rent is currently growing - that is the bull case in one line.
base_case_rationale: No number is recordable, for the same two reasons as on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-23, both still unfixed, and they point in OPPOSITE directions so correcting either alone publishes a confident wrong answer. FLEET CAPEX: capex_series [31.082, 15.631, 5.140] is the 'Purchase of property, equipment and furnishings' line. The Q2 10-Q investing section carries, two lines above it, 'Purchase of equipment held for operating lease and for sale ( 401,934 ) ( 154,944 )' for H1 2026 and H1 2025 against 'Purchase of property, equipment and furnishings ( 6,287 ) ( 17,117 )'. Every engine Willis buys is treated as free, so the $347.6M base is operating cash flow less office furniture. Net of $302.8M of sale proceeds, H1 net fleet investment is about $99M, roughly $210M annualised against a recorded capex mean near $17M. SYNTHETIC COST OF DEBT: the model sets a 14.38% WACC on a lessor with $0.3M of goodwill, because EBIT of $104.3M over interest of $132.1M is 0.79x coverage and the synthetic rating reads distressed - while the rate Willis actually pays is $132,060k over $2,320,904k = 5.69%. For an engine lessor a sub-1x coverage ratio is the business model, not distress: the funding cost of the assets sits below an operating line already struck after their depreciation. The grid from the 2026-09-23 pass is unchanged and I reproduce it: at the engine's base and WACC the market implies +6.1%; correcting capex alone +19.4%; correcting the WACC alone -13.6%; correcting both roughly +1% to +8% - fair against lease rent +6.7% and adjusted EBITDA +4.0%. The schema cannot override WACC, and repricing the corrected ~$211M base through 14.38% prints a fair value near minus $33 a share, so no final_growth is supplied.
key_risks: Gains on sale of leased equipment were $32.0M against $34.0M of total income from operations in Q2 - most of reported operating income is portfolio turnover
New Series B preferred at 8.09% is the marginal cost of capital and sits ahead of the common
Engine lease rates are at a cyclical high driven by GTF inspections and LEAP constraints, both of which are being worked off
$2.32bn of debt against $709M of equity on assets carried at values set in the tightest aftermarket on record
watch_for: Any disclosure splitting maintenance from growth fleet investment - the single input that would make this name modellable
Gains on sale as a share of operating income trending down, which would expose the underlying lease economics
Whether net fleet investment (purchases less sale proceeds) stays near the ~$99M H1 run rate or accelerates
